weak: I will revert back to you by end of day.
strong: I will get back to you by 5 PM.
why: 'Revert' means to return to a previous state, not to reply. 'Revert back' is redundant and a common Indian corporate calque.

skill.work: I'll get back to you by 5 p.m. with the numbers.
skill.everyday: Let me ask my brother and get back to you tonight.
skill.analogy: 'Revert' is the Undo button; 'get back to you' is the Reply button.
skill.insteadOf: I will revert back to you by end of day.

weak: Can we prepone tomorrow's sync?
strong: Can we move tomorrow's sync earlier / bring it forward?
why: 'Prepone' is understood across India but unfamiliar in international boardrooms. 'Move up' or 'bring forward' are standard globally.

skill.work: Can we bring tomorrow's stand-up forward to 9:30?
skill.everyday: Let's move dinner earlier, to seven; the kids have school.
skill.analogy: Like dragging a calendar block up the page: you bring it forward.
skill.insteadOf: Can we prepone tomorrow's sync?

weak: Please do the needful at your end.
strong: Could you please review the attached draft and confirm approval?
why: 'Do the needful' is archaic Victorian English that sounds vague and passive. State the exact requested action directly.

skill.work: Could you sign the form and send it back by noon?
skill.everyday: Could you pick up milk and bread on your way home?
skill.analogy: Like telling an auto driver 'take me somewhere good': name the place instead.
skill.insteadOf: Please do the needful at your end.

weak: I am out of station this week.
strong: I will be traveling / away from my desk this week.
why: 'Out of station' is colonial-era terminology. 'Away from desk', 'traveling', or 'out of office' are modern international standards.

skill.work: I'm travelling this week, so I'll join calls by phone.
skill.everyday: We're away for Diwali, so please pause the newspaper till Monday.
skill.analogy: 'Out of station' is railway talk; outside India people simply say 'away' or 'travelling'.
skill.insteadOf: I am out of station this week.

weak: Let's discuss about the sprint priorities.
strong: Let's discuss the sprint priorities.
why: 'Discuss' is a transitive verb that directly takes an object. Adding 'about' is redundant.

skill.work: Let's discuss the sprint priorities after lunch.
skill.everyday: We discussed the wedding menu over chai.
skill.analogy: 'Discuss' already has the 'about' inside, like chai that already has sugar.
skill.insteadOf: Let's discuss about the sprint priorities.

weak: Tell me one thing, why was this delayed?
strong: Could you help me understand what caused the delay?
why: 'Tell me one thing' is a literal translation of 'ek baat batao' and can sound confrontational in executive meetings.

skill.work: Could you help me understand what held up the release?
skill.everyday: Help me understand: why is the car service taking a week?
skill.analogy: 'Tell me one thing' feels like a cross-examination; 'help me understand' pulls up a chair.
skill.insteadOf: Tell me one thing, why was this delayed?

weak: Same pinch! I was thinking the same thing.
strong: Great minds think alike / We are on the exact same page.
why: 'Same pinch' is schoolyard slang. In professional settings, affirm shared perspective with executive presence.

skill.work: Great minds think alike: I was about to suggest the same fix.
skill.everyday: You ordered masala dosa too? Great minds think alike!
skill.analogy: Like two friends turning up in the same shirt and laughing about it.
skill.insteadOf: Same pinch! I was thinking the same thing.

weak: I have a few doubts on this architecture diagram.
strong: I have a few questions about this architecture diagram.
why: 'Doubt' implies skepticism or mistrust. 'Questions' or 'clarifications' convey constructive curiosity.

skill.work: I have a few questions about this architecture diagram.
skill.everyday: Quick question about the recipe: do I soak the rajma overnight?
skill.analogy: 'I have a doubt' sounds like you suspect a trick; 'a question' is a raised hand.
skill.insteadOf: I have a few doubts on this architecture diagram.

weak: I passed out from IIT Delhi in 2020.
strong: I graduated from IIT Delhi in 2020.
why: 'Pass out' means to faint or lose consciousness in standard English. Use 'graduated' or 'completed my degree'.

skill.work: I graduated from IIT Delhi in 2020 and joined as an analyst.
skill.everyday: My sister graduated last year and now teaches in Pune.
skill.analogy: Outside India, 'passed out' means fainted, so people picture you on the floor.
skill.insteadOf: I passed out from IIT Delhi in 2020.

weak: My cousin brother works in fintech.
strong: My cousin works in fintech.
why: 'Cousin brother' and 'cousin sister' are Indian English coinages. English uses simply 'cousin'.

skill.work: My cousin works in fintech; he might help with the demo.
skill.everyday: My cousin and I grew up in the same lane in Lucknow.
skill.analogy: 'Cousin' already covers brothers and sisters, like 'chai' covers every kind of tea.
skill.insteadOf: My cousin brother works in fintech.

weak: I am giving an exam tomorrow.
strong: I am taking / sitting for an exam tomorrow.
why: In standard English, the teacher *gives* (administers) the exam; the student *takes* or *sits for* the exam.

skill.work: I'm taking my AWS exam on Friday, so I'll log off early.
skill.everyday: My son is taking his maths exam tomorrow.
skill.analogy: The teacher sets the exam and the student takes it, like a bowler bowls and a batter faces.
skill.insteadOf: I am giving an exam tomorrow.

weak: Today morning we had an outage.
strong: This morning we had an outage.
why: Standard English uses 'this morning', 'this afternoon', or 'tonight', never 'today morning'.

skill.work: This morning we had a short outage on the payments page.
skill.everyday: This morning the milkman came at six.
skill.analogy: English says 'this' for today: this morning, this evening, like 'this match' you're watching.
skill.insteadOf: Today morning we had an outage.

weak: Ping me on WhatsApp once you finish.
strong: Drop me a quick update on Slack once you finish.
why: Keeps workplace communication in official searchable channels rather than fragmented personal apps.

skill.work: Drop me a quick update on Slack once the build passes.
skill.everyday: Drop me a message when you reach home.
skill.analogy: Like a note on the office noticeboard everyone checks, not one in your own pocket.
skill.insteadOf: Ping me on WhatsApp once you finish.

weak: Myself Rahul from the frontend team.
strong: I'm Rahul from the frontend team.
why: 'Myself [Name]' is grammatically incorrect in standard English. Reflexive pronouns cannot be sentence subjects.

skill.work: Hi, I'm Rahul from the frontend team.
skill.everyday: Hi, I'm Rahul, Priya's neighbour from the third floor.
skill.analogy: 'Myself' needs an 'I' earlier in the sentence, like an echo needs a shout first.
skill.insteadOf: Myself Rahul from the frontend team.

weak: Kindly arrange a sync for this.
strong: Could you please schedule 15 minutes for us to connect?
why: 'Kindly arrange' is passive bureaucratic phrasing. Specific requests with time estimates convey executive clarity.

skill.work: Could you schedule 15 minutes with Priya this week?
skill.everyday: Could you book a table for six on Saturday?
skill.analogy: 'Kindly arrange' is an old government letter; 'could you' is a friendly WhatsApp.
skill.insteadOf: Kindly arrange a sync for this.

weak: Do one thing, pull the latest branch.
strong: Here's what I suggest: let's pull the latest branch.
why: 'Do one thing' is a direct calque of Hindi 'ek kaam karo'. Professional suggestions land better with collaborative framing.

skill.work: Here's what I suggest: pull the latest branch and rerun the tests.
skill.everyday: Here's an idea: let's take the metro, not an auto.
skill.analogy: 'Do one thing' sounds like an order; 'here's what I suggest' hands over a menu.
skill.insteadOf: Do one thing, pull the latest branch.

weak: Let's sleep over this decision.
strong: Let's sleep on this decision and confirm tomorrow morning.
why: The standard idiom is 'sleep on' (take time overnight to reflect), not 'sleep over' (stay at someone's house).

skill.work: Let's sleep on it and decide at tomorrow's stand-up.
skill.everyday: The flat looks good, but let's sleep on it before we sign.
skill.analogy: Like dosa batter resting overnight: the decision is better in the morning.
skill.insteadOf: Let's sleep over this decision.

weak: Keep me in the loop for any small change.
strong: Please flag any blocking changes or timeline risks to me.
why: Focuses communication on high-signal blockers rather than micro-managing trivial commits.

skill.work: Please flag anything that could move the launch date.
skill.everyday: Message me if the train's late; skip the small updates.
skill.analogy: A smoke alarm rings for fire, not for every cup of chai.
skill.insteadOf: Keep me in the loop for any small change.

weak: You please share the screen.
strong: Would you mind sharing your screen so we can walk through it together?
why: Polite, inclusive framing establishes rapport during virtual technical reviews.

skill.work: Would you mind sharing your screen so we can walk through it?
skill.everyday: Would you mind holding the door for a second?
skill.analogy: 'You please share' is an order in a polite hat; 'would you mind' is a real ask.
skill.insteadOf: You please share the screen.

weak: Am I audible to everyone present?
strong: Can everyone hear me clearly?
why: 'Am I audible' is overly formal and prevalent in Indian teleconferences; 'Can everyone hear me' is natural and direct.

skill.work: Can everyone hear me clearly?
skill.everyday: Can you hear me? I'm on the train.
skill.analogy: 'Am I audible' sounds like an old radio test; 'can you hear me' sounds like today.
skill.insteadOf: Am I audible to everyone present?

weak: Don't pass the blame to the DevOps team.
strong: Let's not pass the buck to DevOps. Let's find the cause together.
why: "Pass the buck" means pushing the blame or the job onto someone else.

skill.work: Let's not pass the buck; let's find what broke and fix it.
skill.everyday: My brothers kept passing the buck about who broke the TV remote.
skill.analogy: Like a hot potato passed round the circle: nobody wants to hold it.
skill.insteadOf: Don't pass the blame to the DevOps team.

weak: Tell me beforehand if server goes down.
strong: Please give me a heads-up before initiating the database migration.
why: 'Give me a heads-up' is natural professional idiom for proactive advance notification.

skill.work: Please give me a heads-up before you start the database migration.
skill.everyday: Give me a heads-up if you're coming for dinner.
skill.analogy: Like honking before a blind turn on a hill road.
skill.insteadOf: Tell me beforehand if server goes down.

weak: Let's close the office work now.
strong: Let's call it a day and pick this up first thing tomorrow.
why: 'Call it a day' is the standard conversational wrap-up phrase when diminishing returns set in.

skill.work: Let's call it a day and pick this up first thing tomorrow.
skill.everyday: We'd painted two walls, so we called it a day.
skill.analogy: Like the umpire calling stumps: play stops, and the match continues tomorrow.
skill.insteadOf: Let's close the office work now.

weak: We will talk about this later sometime.
strong: Let's circle back on this once the A/B test results are finalized.
why: Specifies a clear trigger event for returning to the discussion rather than leaving it unresolved.

skill.work: Let's circle back on this once the test results are in.
skill.everyday: Let's circle back to the holiday plan after Diwali.
skill.analogy: Like a lap around the block: you come back to the same spot later.
skill.insteadOf: We will talk about this later sometime.

weak: I want to speak with you for two minutes.
strong: Let's touch base for five minutes before the client demo.
why: 'Touch base' crisply signals a brief alignment check without implying an escalation.

skill.work: Let's touch base for five minutes before the client demo.
skill.everyday: I'll touch base with the landlord about the leak tomorrow.
skill.analogy: Like a batter touching the crease between runs: a quick check-in, then go.
skill.insteadOf: I want to speak with you for two minutes.

weak: This deadline is totally impossible for my team.
strong: If we keep Friday, we'll have to skip testing. Could we move it to Tuesday?
why: Give the fact and an option, not a complaint.

skill.work: At our current pace, Friday means cutting testing. Can we say Tuesday?
skill.everyday: If we leave at six, we'll miss the start. Can we go at five?
skill.analogy: Like telling the cook the oven fits one tray, not three: facts, not complaints.
skill.insteadOf: This deadline is totally impossible for my team.

weak: Stop talking about this in the group call.
strong: Let's take this offline so we can keep today's review focused on core roadmap items.
why: Politely parks tangent discussions without invalidating the team member.

skill.work: Let's take this offline so today's review stays on the roadmap.
skill.everyday: Let's take the trip debate offline; I'll call you after dinner.
skill.analogy: Like moving a side argument out of the wedding hall into the corridor.
skill.insteadOf: Stop talking about this in the group call.

weak: I have too much pending work to take this.
strong: I don't have the bandwidth this sprint without trading off the payments milestone.
why: Demonstrates prioritization maturity by explicitly linking capacity to trade-offs.

skill.work: I don't have the bandwidth this sprint unless we move the payments work.
skill.everyday: I don't have the bandwidth to plan the reunion this month.
skill.analogy: Like a phone data pack: once it's used up, nothing new loads.
skill.insteadOf: I have too much pending work to take this.

weak: We are not matching our thoughts.
strong: Let's align on the acceptance criteria before opening PRs.
why: Replaces vague emotional misalignment with concrete technical milestones.

skill.work: Let's align on what 'done' means before anyone opens a pull request.
skill.everyday: Let's align on the area before we visit any flats.
skill.analogy: Like agreeing on the destination before you book the cab.
skill.insteadOf: We are not matching our thoughts.

weak: Give me some rough guess for timing.
strong: Could you share a ballpark estimate for the auth refactor?
why: 'Ballpark estimate' clearly requests order-of-magnitude sizing without demanding premature precision.

skill.work: Could you give me a ballpark figure for the login rework?
skill.everyday: Ballpark, how long is the drive to Mysuru?
skill.analogy: Like a shopkeeper's 'around two kilos' before he puts it on the scale.
skill.insteadOf: Give me some rough guess for timing.

weak: There can be big issues later.
strong: I want to flag a risk with this design before we build it.
why: "Flag" calmly points out a risk early, so people can act on it.

skill.work: I want to flag a risk with the new login flow before Friday.
skill.everyday: Just flagging: the road to the venue floods when it rains.
skill.analogy: Like a railway guard waving a red flag before the train reaches trouble.
skill.insteadOf: There can be big issues later.

weak: Did that issue get solved or what?
strong: Just closing the loop on the memory leak we diagnosed yesterday.
why: 'Closing the loop' communicates disciplined operational closure.

skill.work: Just closing the loop: the memory leak is fixed and live.
skill.everyday: Closing the loop: the plumber came and the tap's fixed.
skill.analogy: Like texting 'reached home' after a friend asked you to message when you got in.
skill.insteadOf: Did that issue get solved or what?

weak: I have to leave right now at 4.
strong: I have a hard stop at 4:00 PM for an architectural review.
why: Clearly sets boundaries in advance so meetings don't spill over.

skill.work: I have a hard stop at 4 p.m., so let's start with the risks.
skill.everyday: I have a hard stop at eight; it's my niece's birthday.
skill.analogy: Like the last metro: it leaves at eleven, whether you're on it or not.
skill.insteadOf: I have to leave right now at 4.

weak: What is the main thing you learned from this?
strong: My primary takeaway is that user drop-off is driven by onboarding latency.
why: 'Takeaway' isolates the actionable thesis from pages of raw data.

skill.work: My main takeaway: users drop off because sign-up is slow.
skill.everyday: My main takeaway from the trip: never book the 6 a.m. flight.
skill.analogy: Like the one line you still remember from a film after leaving the theatre.
skill.insteadOf: What is the main thing you learned from this?

weak: This will help our product a lot.
strong: Optimizing cold-start latency will directly move the needle on user retention.
why: 'Move the needle' specifies meaningful, measurable impact on key business metrics.

skill.work: A faster start-up time will really move the needle on retention.
skill.everyday: Skipping evening tea really moved the needle on my sleep.
skill.analogy: Like a speedometer: only a real push makes the needle climb.
skill.insteadOf: This will help our product a lot.

weak: Let's do the easy small tasks first.
strong: Let's pick off the low-hanging fruit while design finishes the mockups.
why: "Low-hanging fruit" means the easy wins you can get quickly.

skill.work: Let's fix the low-hanging fruit first, like the broken links.
skill.everyday: Cleaning the fridge is the low-hanging fruit before Diwali guests arrive.
skill.analogy: The mangoes you can pick by hand before anyone fetches a ladder.
skill.insteadOf: Let's do the easy small tasks first.

weak: Let's stop talking on this right now.
strong: Can we park this until we have the data from production?
why: "Park" means pause it and come back later; "table" means opposite things in the UK and US.

skill.work: Let's park this until we have the production data.
skill.everyday: Let's park the holiday plan until the exam results are out.
skill.analogy: Like parking a car: it waits safely till you come back.
skill.insteadOf: Let's stop talking on this right now.

weak: Look more deeply into the numbers.
strong: Let's drill down into the p99 latency spikes occurring between 2 and 4 PM.
why: Signals focused analytical investigation into specific root anomalies.

skill.work: Let's drill down into the slow pages between 2 and 4 p.m.
skill.everyday: When we drilled down into the electricity bill, the geyser was the culprit.
skill.analogy: Like digging a borewell: one spot, deeper and deeper.
skill.insteadOf: Look more deeply into the numbers.

weak: Don't try to build every single feature on day one.
strong: Let's not bite off more than we can chew in version one. Core features first.
why: A common idiom for taking on more than you can handle at once.

skill.work: Let's not bite off more than we can chew; ship the core first.
skill.everyday: We bit off more than we could chew: twenty guests and one small oven.
skill.analogy: Like cooking for the whole colony when six friends are coming over.
skill.insteadOf: Don't try to build every single feature on day one.

weak: Clean the user input before saving.
strong: Ensure we sanitize and validate all payload parameters at the ingress boundary.
why: Precise engineering vocabulary for input security and defensive coding.

skill.work: We sanitise all user input before saving it.
skill.everyday: We sanitised the kitchen counters after the cooking class.
skill.analogy: Like washing vegetables from the market before they go in the pot.
skill.insteadOf: Clean the user input before saving.

weak: Jumping between different tickets is making me tired.
strong: All this context switching between support and project work is slowing us down.
why: "Context switching" means jumping between tasks and losing time at every jump.

skill.work: Constant context switching between support and features is slowing the team down.
skill.everyday: Cooking while helping with homework is too much context switching for me.
skill.analogy: Like changing trains every two stations: you spend the whole trip on platforms.
skill.insteadOf: Jumping between different tickets is making me tired.

weak: Explain that specific point in more detail.
strong: Can we dig into that last point a bit more?
why: "Dig into" means look at it closely; "double-click on" is jargon many listeners find odd.

skill.work: Let's dig into why staging and production numbers differ.
skill.everyday: Let me dig into why the electricity bill doubled this month.
skill.analogy: Like zooming into one corner of a map until the street names show.
skill.insteadOf: Explain that specific point in more detail.

weak: I am arguing just to oppose your idea.
strong: Playing devil's advocate for a moment: what happens if the third-party webhook fails silently?
why: Invites rigorous stress-testing of assumptions without personal animus.

skill.work: Let me play devil's advocate: what if the payment webhook fails silently?
skill.everyday: Playing devil's advocate: do we really need a bigger car?
skill.analogy: Like the friend who argues for the other team just to test your cricket opinion.
skill.insteadOf: I am arguing just to oppose your idea.

weak: Are we thinking identical things?
strong: I want to ensure we're on the same page regarding the rollout sequence.
why: Standard executive check to ensure cross-functional understanding before kickoff.

skill.work: Just to make sure we're on the same page about the rollout order.
skill.everyday: Are we on the same page about leaving at six?
skill.analogy: Like the whole class turning to page 42 before the teacher starts.
skill.insteadOf: Are we thinking identical things?

weak: We need to get their agreement.
strong: We need stakeholder buy-in before freezing the quarterly roadmap.
why: Captures genuine alignment and commitment rather than passive compliance.

skill.work: We need the sales team's buy-in before we freeze the roadmap.
skill.everyday: Get the kids' buy-in before you book the trek.
skill.analogy: Like getting everyone at home to agree on the film before buying tickets.
skill.insteadOf: We need to get their agreement.

weak: I will teach them how to run this code.
strong: I will schedule a knowledge transfer session with the on-call team before handoff.
why: Standard formal term for structured operational training and documentation handover.

skill.work: I'll run a knowledge transfer session with the support team on Friday.
skill.everyday: Before Nani left, she did a knowledge transfer on her pickle recipe.
skill.analogy: Like a relay runner handing over the baton, not just pointing at it.
skill.insteadOf: I will teach them how to run this code.

weak: Who will do what now?
strong: Let's recap the agreed action items and owners before we adjourn.
why: Drives meeting accountability with clear assignments and delivery expectations.

skill.work: Quick recap of action items: Riya owns testing, I own the release.
skill.everyday: So: I'll book tickets, you pack snacks, Arjun brings the car.
skill.analogy: Like the tiffin list on the fridge: one name next to each dish.
skill.insteadOf: Who will do what now?

weak: Tell if you are unhappy with the plan.
strong: Please surface any architectural concerns early so we can adapt the design doc.
why: Encourages proactive, blameless feedback during early design phases.

skill.work: Please raise any concerns early so we can change the design.
skill.everyday: If the trip plan worries you, raise it now, not at the station.
skill.analogy: Like pointing out the crack in the wall before the painters start.
skill.insteadOf: Tell if you are unhappy with the plan.

weak: Spend only 3 hours on this experiment.
strong: Let's timebox this spike to three hours; if unresolved, we escalate to the lead.
why: Prevents rabbit holes and enforces disciplined research spikes.

skill.work: Let's timebox this to three hours; if it's still stuck, we ask Priya.
skill.everyday: I timebox WhatsApp to ten minutes after dinner.
skill.analogy: Like a pressure cooker: three whistles and you switch it off, done or not.
skill.insteadOf: Spend only 3 hours on this experiment.

weak: Let everyone remember the background first.
strong: Let me quickly get everyone up to speed before we start the updates.
why: "Up to speed" means knowing the latest; "level-set" is jargon outside some offices.

skill.work: Let's get everyone up to speed on Q3 goals before the updates.
skill.everyday: Let me get Dad up to speed before he calls the builder.
skill.analogy: Like a quick recap of the last episode before the new one starts.
skill.insteadOf: Let everyone remember the background first.

weak: Fix all the small remaining problems.
strong: We have a few minor styling edge cases to iron out before the client demo.
why: Conversational idiom for smoothing out minor rough spots in an otherwise solid build.

skill.work: We have a few small styling issues to iron out before the demo.
skill.everyday: We still need to iron out who's driving to the wedding.
skill.analogy: Like pressing the last few creases out of a shirt before you leave.
skill.insteadOf: Fix all the small remaining problems.

weak: Our main top aim for this product.
strong: Our north star metric is reducing mean time to recovery during incidents.
why: Provides an unambiguous primary indicator of team success.

skill.work: Our north star is faster recovery whenever something breaks.
skill.everyday: My north star this year is running the Mumbai marathon.
skill.analogy: Like the Pole Star sailors steer by: one fixed point for every decision.
skill.insteadOf: Our main top aim for this product.

weak: The best balanced point between two things.
strong: This architecture hits the sweet spot between low cost and sub-second latency.
why: Describes optimal trade-off resolution where competing forces balance out.

skill.work: This design hits the sweet spot between low cost and speed.
skill.everyday: Ten in the morning is the sweet spot: no rush, shops already open.
skill.analogy: The middle of the bat: hit it there and the ball flies.
skill.insteadOf: The best balanced point between two things.

weak: Check if this calculation makes sense.
strong: Let me do a quick sanity check on these database read replica IOPS figures.
why: Informal verification to confirm that numbers or logic are plausible before publishing.

skill.work: Let me do a quick sanity check on these numbers before we send them.
skill.everyday: Quick sanity check: is 4 a.m. too early to leave for Goa?
skill.analogy: Like tasting the dal for salt before you serve it.
skill.insteadOf: Check if this calculation makes sense.

weak: This tool will solve all our problems instantly.
strong: Kubernetes is powerful, but it is not a silver bullet for poor application architecture.
why: Classic warning against the illusion of effortless, all-encompassing technical panaceas.

skill.work: The new tool helps, but it isn't a silver bullet for slow pages.
skill.everyday: Green tea isn't a silver bullet; you still need to walk.
skill.analogy: Like hoping one new bat will fix your whole batting technique.
skill.insteadOf: This tool will solve all our problems instantly.

weak: Where is the work getting stuck right now?
strong: Manual QA validation has become the primary bottleneck in our release cadence.
why: Identifies systemic throughput constraints rather than blaming individuals.

skill.work: Manual testing has become the bottleneck in our release.
skill.everyday: The single billing counter is the bottleneck on Saturdays.
skill.analogy: Like the one-lane bridge on a highway: everything waits there.
skill.insteadOf: Where is the work getting stuck right now?

weak: Try something very daring and advanced.
strong: This prototype pushes the envelope on real-time on-device audio transcription.
why: Recognizes innovative engineering that expands existing technical boundaries.

skill.work: This prototype pushes the envelope on voice typing in Hindi.
skill.everyday: Her fusion biryani really pushes the envelope.
skill.analogy: Like a test pilot flying a little faster than anyone has before.
skill.insteadOf: Try something very daring and advanced.

weak: We made a silly mistake on our side.
strong: We dropped the ball on notifying the client ahead of the scheduled maintenance window.
why: Accepts clear, unevasive organizational accountability without deflecting.

skill.work: We dropped the ball on telling the client about the downtime.
skill.everyday: I dropped the ball on Mum's birthday cake; I forgot to order it.
skill.analogy: Like a fielder dropping an easy catch: own it and move on.
skill.insteadOf: We made a silly mistake on our side.

weak: We will change our whole direction now.
strong: Based on early conversion data, we are pivoting our strategy toward enterprise tier accounts.
why: Communicates deliberate strategic agility grounded in market evidence.

skill.work: Based on early data, we're pivoting towards larger business customers.
skill.everyday: The café pivoted from dine-in to delivery during the monsoon.
skill.analogy: Like a basketball player keeping one foot planted and turning to face a new direction.
skill.insteadOf: We will change our whole direction now.

weak: They must also face risk if this fails.
strong: Having engineering leads carry the on-call pager ensures real skin in the game for reliability.
why: Conveys genuine shared stakes and aligned incentives.

skill.work: When leads carry the on-call phone, they have real skin in the game.
skill.everyday: Everyone chipped in for the trip, so everyone has skin in the game.
skill.analogy: Like a cook who eats his own food: he cares how it tastes.
skill.insteadOf: They must also face risk if this fails.

weak: Kindly adjust with the delay.
strong: Thanks for bearing with the delay — the fix will be live by 6 PM.
why: 'Kindly adjust' asks for vague patience; stating the time and thanking them is concrete and warm.

skill.work: Thanks for bearing with the delay; the fix will be live by six.
skill.everyday: Thanks for bearing with us; the guests are running late.
skill.analogy: 'Kindly adjust' asks them to squeeze in; 'thanks for bearing with us' offers chai while they wait.
skill.insteadOf: Kindly adjust with the delay.

weak: What is your good name?
strong: May I have your name, please?
why: 'Good name' translates an Indian courtesy formula that confuses foreigners; the plain version works everywhere.

skill.work: Before we start, may I have your name, please?
skill.everyday: Hi, what's your name? I'm Riya, Priya's friend.
skill.analogy: 'Good name' is 'shubh naam' translated word for word; English just says 'name'.
skill.insteadOf: What is your good name?

weak: I told him yesterday itself.
strong: I already told him yesterday.
why: Trailing 'itself' and 'only' for emphasis are common in Indian English; plain time words carry the meaning cleanly.

skill.work: I already told him yesterday; he's working on it.
skill.everyday: Mum fixed the leak the same day; she didn't wait.
skill.analogy: 'Itself' after a time word is extra salt; English adds 'already' or 'the same day'.
skill.insteadOf: I told him yesterday itself.

weak: I am on leave for my cousin's marriage.
strong: I am on leave for my cousin's wedding.
why: 'Marriage' is the institution; 'wedding' is the event you attend.

skill.work: I'm on leave next Friday for my cousin's wedding.
skill.everyday: We danced all night at my cousin's wedding.
skill.analogy: A wedding is the party day; a marriage is the years after it.
skill.insteadOf: I am on leave for my cousin's marriage.

weak: I am shifting my house this weekend.
strong: I am moving house this weekend.
why: 'Shifting' for relocation is Indian usage; international listeners expect 'moving'.

skill.work: I'm moving house this weekend, so I'll be offline on Saturday.
skill.everyday: We're moving house in May, to a flat near the metro.
skill.analogy: You shift gears or furniture; you move house.
skill.insteadOf: I am shifting my house this weekend.

weak: He is my real brother, not cousin.
strong: He's my brother, not a cousin.
why: One word covers it: 'brother'. Add 'not a cousin' only when that distinction is the point.

skill.work: Yes, Arjun in sales is my brother, not a cousin.
skill.everyday: That's my brother; my cousins are the ones near the stage.
skill.analogy: 'Brother' already means real; adding 'real' makes listeners wonder about the fake ones.
skill.insteadOf: He is my real brother, not cousin.

weak: Please join as per your convenience.
strong: Please join any time before Friday that suits you.
why: 'As per your convenience' is stiff circular-office English; a plain time window is warmer and clearer.

skill.work: Join any time before Friday that suits you.
skill.everyday: Come over whenever it suits you this weekend.
skill.analogy: 'As per your convenience' is a stamped circular; 'whenever suits you' is a phone call.
skill.insteadOf: Please join as per your convenience.

weak: Please note the same and confirm.
strong: Please confirm once you have updated the sheet.
why: 'The same' as a pronoun is babu-English; naming the thing keeps the ask sharp.

skill.work: Please confirm once you've updated the sheet.
skill.everyday: Let me know once you've booked the tickets.
skill.analogy: 'The same' as a pronoun is a dusty file cabinet; just name the thing.
skill.insteadOf: Please note the same and confirm.

weak: Kindly intimate the team about the change.
strong: Please inform the team about the change today.
why: 'Intimate' as a verb for informing is archaic officialese; 'inform' or 'tell' is current.

skill.work: Please let the team know about the change today.
skill.everyday: Let Mum know we'll be late for dinner.
skill.analogy: To global ears, 'intimate the team' sounds romantic, not like sending an email.
skill.insteadOf: Kindly intimate the team about the change.

weak: I will take my dinner late.
strong: I will have dinner late.
why: 'Take dinner' is a direct translation; 'have dinner' is the natural collocation.

skill.work: I'll have dinner late, so let's take the call at eight.
skill.everyday: We usually have dinner at nine on weekends.
skill.analogy: You take medicine; you have dinner.
skill.insteadOf: I will take my dinner late.

weak: Please open the light.
strong: Please switch on the light.
why: Lights and fans are 'switched on', not 'opened'; 'open' applies to doors and windows.

skill.work: Could someone switch on the lights in the meeting room?
skill.everyday: Please switch on the fan; it's hot.
skill.analogy: You open doors and windows; lights and fans you switch on.
skill.insteadOf: Please open the light.

weak: Close the TV, please.
strong: Switch off the TV, please.
why: Devices are 'switched off'; 'close' is for apps, tabs, and doors.

skill.work: Please switch off the projector when you leave.
skill.everyday: Switch off the TV and come for dinner.
skill.analogy: You close a tap; a TV you switch off or turn off.
skill.insteadOf: Close the TV, please.

weak: I can't come to the review.
strong: I won't be able to make the review — but I've shared my update in the doc.
why: A reason plus a contribution softens the no and keeps you visible.

skill.work: I can't make the review, but my update is in the doc.
skill.everyday: I can't make lunch on Sunday, but I'm free for chai on Monday.
skill.analogy: A 'no' with a door left open, so they don't feel shut out.
skill.insteadOf: I can't come to the review.

weak: No, I can't take this up.
strong: I can't give this proper attention this week; I can start Monday.
why: Refusing the timing instead of the work keeps the door open and the quality promise intact.

skill.work: I can't give this proper attention this week; I can start Monday.
skill.everyday: I can't help this weekend, but I'm free next Saturday.
skill.analogy: Like a clinic receptionist: not today, but here's the next free slot.
skill.insteadOf: No, I can't take this up.

weak: That won't be possible.
strong: That won't be possible in this timeline — here's what we can do instead.
why: A no followed by an option turns a wall into a choice.

skill.work: That won't work by Friday; here's what we can do by then.
skill.everyday: Saturday's packed, but how about Sunday brunch?
skill.analogy: A closed road with a diversion sign is easier to take than a dead end.
skill.insteadOf: That won't be possible.

weak: This is too much for the timeline.
strong: To hold the date, I'd suggest we ship the core flow first and phase the reports.
why: Naming what survives the cut makes pushback sound like planning, not complaining.

skill.work: To hold the date, let's ship the core flow first and add reports later.
skill.everyday: To reach by seven, let's skip the dhaba stop and eat there.
skill.analogy: Like packing for a short trip: carry the essentials, send the rest later.
skill.insteadOf: This is too much for the timeline.

weak: If we rush this, quality will suffer.
strong: Rushing this risks a buggy release — can we take two more days for testing?
why: Attaching the risk to the customer outcome makes the delay defensible.

skill.work: Rushing this risks a buggy release. Can we take two more days to test?
skill.everyday: If we rush the paint, it'll peel by the monsoon. Can we wait a day?
skill.analogy: Like taking a cake out early: it looks done, then sinks in the middle.
skill.insteadOf: If we rush this, quality will suffer.

weak: I don't agree with this plan.
strong: I see it differently — can I share a concern about the rollout order?
why: Asking permission to differ lowers defences before the disagreement lands.

skill.work: I see it differently; can I share a concern about the rollout order?
skill.everyday: I see it differently: the earlier train gets us there before the rush.
skill.analogy: Like pointing to another route on the map, not grabbing the steering wheel.
skill.insteadOf: I don't agree with this plan.

weak: You are wrong about the numbers.
strong: The dashboard shows a different picture — shall we look at it together?
why: Pointing at shared data removes the personal sting from the correction.

skill.work: The dashboard shows a different picture; shall we look at it together?
skill.everyday: The app says the shop closes at nine; shall we check before driving?
skill.analogy: Like checking the scoreboard together instead of arguing about the score.
skill.insteadOf: You are wrong about the numbers.

weak: Sorry, but let me speak.
strong: Can I pause you there? I want to build on that point.
why: Framing the interruption as building, not blocking, keeps the room warm.

skill.work: Can I pause you there? I want to build on that point.
skill.everyday: Can I stop you there? That's exactly what happened to me!
skill.analogy: A gentle tap on the shoulder, not a shout across the room.
skill.insteadOf: Sorry, but let me speak.

weak: I didn't understand anything.
strong: I followed the first half — could you walk through the second half again?
why: Showing where you got lost invites a targeted answer instead of a full repeat.

skill.work: I followed the first half; could you walk me through the API part again?
skill.everyday: I got the first turn; can you repeat the directions after the temple?
skill.analogy: Like telling the mechanic which noise, not just 'the car is bad'.
skill.insteadOf: I didn't understand anything.

weak: The work is stuck because of them.
strong: I'm blocked on the API keys — I've pinged Arjun twice; can you nudge him?
why: Naming the blocker and the attempts turns blame into a clear ask.

skill.work: I'm blocked on the API keys. I've pinged Arjun twice; can you nudge him?
skill.everyday: We're stuck on the gas connection; can you call the agency once?
skill.analogy: Like telling the guard which signal is red and who can turn it green.
skill.insteadOf: The work is stuck because of them.

weak: Almost done with my part.
strong: My part is done except final testing, which finishes tomorrow.
why: 'Almost done' hides the remainder; naming it builds trust in the date.

skill.work: My part's done except final testing, which finishes tomorrow.
skill.everyday: Dinner's ready except the rotis; five minutes.
skill.analogy: Like a delivery app: 'arriving in 5 minutes' beats 'on the way'.
skill.insteadOf: Almost done with my part.

weak: Sorry for the delay.
strong: Sorry for the delay — the report will be with you by 4 PM today.
why: An apology without a time is just noise; the time is the apology.

skill.work: Sorry for the delay; the report will be with you by 4 p.m.
skill.everyday: Sorry I'm late; I'll be there by 7:15.
skill.analogy: Like a train announcement: sorry for the delay, arriving 7:15. The time calms people.
skill.insteadOf: Sorry for the delay.

weak: Thanks for your help.
strong: Thanks for staying back to fix the deploy — we shipped because of it.
why: Specific thanks get remembered; generic thanks evaporate.

skill.work: Thanks for staying back to fix the deploy; we shipped because of you.
skill.everyday: Thanks for the lift to the station; I'd have missed my train.
skill.analogy: A specific thank-you is a handwritten note; 'thanks for your help' is a printed card.
skill.insteadOf: Thanks for your help.

weak: Give me an intro to your manager.
strong: Would you be comfortable introducing me to your manager? Happy to share a blurb.
why: Offering the blurb removes the awkward drafting work from the favour.

skill.work: Would you be comfortable introducing me to your manager? I can send a short note.
skill.everyday: Could you introduce me to your plumber? I'll mention your name.
skill.analogy: Like handing over a gift already wrapped, so passing it on is easy.
skill.insteadOf: Give me an intro to your manager.

weak: Just reminding you about my mail.
strong: Following up on my note from Tuesday — could you confirm by tomorrow?
why: Referencing the date and asking for a day makes the nudge actionable.

skill.work: Following up on my note from Tuesday; could you confirm by tomorrow?
skill.everyday: Following up on the sofa repair: can you come on Saturday morning?
skill.analogy: Like a second knock with your name: 'It's Rahul, from Tuesday.'
skill.insteadOf: Just reminding you about my mail.

weak: I will join late.
strong: I'll join 10 minutes late — please start without me; I'll catch up on the notes.
why: Releasing the room from waiting removes the guilt and the stall.

skill.work: I'll join 10 minutes late; please start without me.
skill.everyday: Running 15 minutes late; order for me, I'll have the thali.
skill.analogy: Like a train app showing '10 min late', so nobody waits on the platform guessing.
skill.insteadOf: I will join late.

weak: I have to leave early today.
strong: I need to leave at 4 today — my reviews are done and Rahul is covering support.
why: Showing cover arranged answers the unspoken question before it is asked.

skill.work: I need to leave at 4 today; Rahul is covering support.
skill.everyday: I'll leave the party at nine; Arjun will drop Nani home.
skill.analogy: Like handing over the car keys before you leave, so nobody is stuck.
skill.insteadOf: I have to leave early today.

weak: Good job on the presentation.
strong: Your opening story made the whole presentation land — the room woke up for it.
why: Praising the specific move teaches; praising the whole teaches nothing.

skill.work: Your opening story made the presentation land; the room woke up.
skill.everyday: That rasam was spot on; the pepper was perfect.
skill.analogy: Pointing at the exact six you loved beats saying 'nice innings'.
skill.insteadOf: Good job on the presentation.

weak: Today I will present my slides.
strong: In the next ten minutes, I'll show you why sign-ups dropped and the one fix I'd try.
why: Promising a finding usually lands better than announcing your slides.

skill.work: In ten minutes, I'll show why sign-ups dropped and one fix to try.
skill.everyday: Quick plan for Sunday: temple at nine, lunch at Nani's, home by four.
skill.analogy: Like a cab driver telling you the route before starting, so you relax.
skill.insteadOf: Today I will present my slides.

weak: I don't know the answer to that.
strong: I don't have that number on me — I'll confirm by tomorrow morning.
why: Admitting the gap plus a time converts a stumble into reliability.

skill.work: I don't have that number on me; I'll confirm by tomorrow morning.
skill.everyday: Not sure when the shop opens; I'll check and text you.
skill.analogy: Like a shopkeeper out of stock saying 'tomorrow by noon', not just 'no'.
skill.insteadOf: I don't know the answer to that.

weak: That's all from my side.
strong: So the ask is two testers for a week — happy to take questions.
why: Ending on the ask tells the room what to do with everything it just heard.

skill.work: So the ask is two testers for one week; happy to take questions.
skill.everyday: So, who's in for Sunday? I need numbers by tonight.
skill.analogy: Like the last over: finish with the winning shot, not a dot ball.
skill.insteadOf: That's all from my side.

weak: I can't come, sorry.
strong: I can't make it tonight — you guys go ahead, and tell me the gossip tomorrow.
why: Releasing friends from waiting plus asking for the story keeps you in the group.

skill.work: Riya: "Team lunch today?" You: "Can't make it, I'm on a client call. Tell me how the new place is?"
skill.everyday: Arjun: "Movie tonight?" You: "Can't make it, you guys go ahead. Tell me the gossip tomorrow!"
skill.analogy: A 'no' with a hook is a door left ajar: they can knock again.
skill.insteadOf: I can't come, sorry.

weak: You should just quit.
strong: If it were me, I'd talk to the manager once before deciding — want to rehearse it?
why: Advice plus an offer of help beats a verdict from the sidelines.

skill.work: Priya: "I'm thinking of switching teams." You: "If it were me, I'd talk to my lead first. Want to think it through over chai?"
skill.everyday: Riya: "My landlord won't fix the leak." You: "If it were me, I'd send him a photo and a date. Want help writing it?"
skill.analogy: Like offering your bike, not riding it for them.
skill.insteadOf: You should just quit.

weak: Don't worry about it.
strong: That sounds rough — do you want advice or just someone to listen?
why: Asking which one they need stops you giving the wrong kind of comfort.

skill.work: Arjun: "The demo crashed in front of the client." You: "That sounds rough. Want ideas, or just to vent for a bit?"
skill.everyday: Riya: "My flight got cancelled." You: "Ugh, that sounds rough. Do you want help rebooking, or just to rant?"
skill.analogy: Like asking if someone wants tea or water before you pour.
skill.insteadOf: Don't worry about it.

weak: You pay, I'll pay next time.
strong: Let's split it now — UPI takes ten seconds and nobody keeps score.
why: Settling on the spot kills the slow poison of remembered debts.

skill.work: Let's split the slides now: I'll take one to five, you take the rest.
skill.everyday: Let's split it now; UPI takes ten seconds.
skill.analogy: Settling now is like clearing the table after dinner: no pile-up tomorrow.
skill.insteadOf: You pay, I'll pay next time.

weak: Do this work properly.
strong: Please mop the bedrooms first today — guests are coming at six.
why: Order plus reason gets cooperation; bare orders get minimum effort.

skill.work: Please test the login page first today; the client demo is at six.
skill.everyday: Please mop the bedrooms first today; guests are coming at six.
skill.analogy: Like giving the auto driver a landmark, not just 'that side'.
skill.insteadOf: Do this work properly.

weak: How much to go there?
strong: Station road — by meter, please? Last time it was eighty rupees.
why: Naming the meter and the last fare sets the terms before the ride starts.

skill.work: Same format as last month's report, please? That one worked well.
skill.everyday: Station Road, by meter, please? Last time it was eighty rupees.
skill.analogy: Like showing the tailor an old shirt that fits: a reference ends the guessing.
skill.insteadOf: How much to go there?

weak: This is defective, take it back.
strong: This stopped working in two days — I'd like a replacement or refund, please.
why: Stating the fact and the remedy keeps the counter on your side.

skill.work: The new laptop crashed twice today; I'd like a replacement, please.
skill.everyday: This kettle stopped working in two days; I'd like a refund, please.
skill.analogy: Like ordering at a counter: name the dish, don't describe your hunger.
skill.insteadOf: This is defective, take it back.

weak: Your voice is breaking.
strong: You're breaking up — could you move to a window or call back?
why: "Breaking up" is the natural phrase; "your voice is breaking" usually means a teenager's voice changing.

skill.work: You're breaking up; could you move closer to the window?
skill.everyday: Mum, you're breaking up; I'll call you back from the balcony.
skill.analogy: Like a radio between stations: the words arrive in pieces.
skill.insteadOf: Your voice is breaking.

weak: My mobile is getting off.
strong: My phone is dying — I'll call back from my laptop if it drops.
why: Phones 'die' or 'run out'; 'getting off' confuses listeners.

skill.work: My phone's dying; I'll rejoin from my laptop if it drops.
skill.everyday: My phone's about to die; I'll text you when I'm home.
skill.analogy: In English a phone 'dies', like a torch fading out; it never 'gets off'.
skill.insteadOf: My mobile is getting off.

weak: Please reply soon.
strong: Could you reply by Thursday? The client review is on Friday.
why: A date plus the reason gets replies; 'soon' gets forgotten.

skill.work: Could you reply by Thursday? The client review is on Friday.
skill.everyday: Can you confirm by tonight? The caterer needs numbers tomorrow.
skill.analogy: Like a date on a train ticket: people plan around it.
skill.insteadOf: Please reply soon.

weak: Regards, please find attached.
strong: Attached: the March invoice (Rs 42,000) — please approve by Friday.
why: Leading with what it is and what you need beats burying both under 'please find'.

skill.work: Attached: the March report, for your sign-off by Friday.
skill.everyday: Photos attached: Diwali at Nani's. Pick your favourite for the album!
skill.analogy: Like a label on a tiffin box: you know what's inside before opening it.
skill.insteadOf: Regards, please find attached.

weak: I am on leave, call someone else.
strong: I'm on leave till Monday — for anything urgent, please call Rahul at 98xxx.
why: A return date plus one named backup is the whole job of a leave note.

skill.work: I'm on leave till Monday; for anything urgent, please call Rahul.
skill.everyday: We're away till Sunday; the spare key is with Mrs Iyer.
skill.analogy: Like a shop sign saying 'Back at 4, ask next door', not just 'Closed'.
skill.insteadOf: I am on leave, call someone else.

weak: Do it fast.
strong: Could you get this back by 3 PM? The client call is at four.
why: A time plus the reason turns pressure into shared urgency.

skill.work: Could you get this back to me by 3 p.m.? The call is at four.
skill.everyday: Can you pick up the cake by six? The party starts at seven.
skill.analogy: 'Do it fast' is a honk; a time and a reason is a clear signboard.
skill.insteadOf: Do it fast.

weak: Well done, keep it up.
strong: Well done on the client summary — crisp, honest about risks, and on time.
why: Naming what was good tells them what to repeat.

skill.work: Well done on the client summary: crisp, honest about risks, and on time.
skill.everyday: Great job on the science project; the labels made it so clear.
skill.analogy: A coach saying 'great cover drive' teaches more than 'good batting'.
skill.insteadOf: Well done, keep it up.

weak: That's wrong.
strong: Almost — the total is right but the March row is last year's. Fix that and we're done.
why: Placing the correction inside what is right keeps the person with you.

skill.work: Almost: the total's right, but the March row is last year's.
skill.everyday: Nearly there: the dal's perfect, it just needs a pinch of salt.
skill.analogy: Like a GPS saying 'turn left in 200 metres', not 'wrong way'.
skill.insteadOf: That's wrong.

weak: Okay then, bye all.
strong: So Rahul owns the API fix by Wednesday — thanks all, see you at standup.
why: Closing with owner plus date is the only part anyone will remember tomorrow.

skill.work: So Rahul owns the API fix by Wednesday. Thanks, all; see you at stand-up.
skill.everyday: So I'm booking the tickets tonight, and you sort out the hotel. Done!
skill.analogy: Like the umpire's final signal: everyone knows the result before leaving the ground.
skill.insteadOf: Okay then, bye all.

weak: How are you? Busy?
strong: How was your weekend — did the match live up to the hype?
why: One specific question opens people up; generic ones get generic answers.

skill.work: You: "How was your weekend? Did the match live up to the hype?" Arjun: "Totally! That last over!"
skill.everyday: You: "How was the wedding? Did the sangeet go on late?" Riya: "Till 2 a.m.!"
skill.analogy: A specific question is a ball bowled to them; 'Busy?' is a dead ball.
skill.insteadOf: How are you? Busy?

weak: Why did you leave your last job?
strong: Are you comfortable sharing what made you move on?
why: "Are you comfortable sharing…" asks a personal question but leaves room to say no.

skill.work: Are you comfortable sharing why the launch moved?
skill.everyday: Are you comfortable sharing how you prepared for the exam?
skill.analogy: Like knocking before you enter: the question leaves them free to say no.
skill.insteadOf: Why did you leave your last job?

weak: I reject this offer.
strong: Thanks for the offer — the timing isn't right for me, but I'd love to stay in touch.
why: Warm declines keep doors open; cold ones close industries.

skill.work: Thanks for the offer; the timing isn't right, but I'd love to stay in touch.
skill.everyday: Thanks for inviting us; we can't make it this time, but next Diwali?
skill.analogy: Like declining a second helping but praising the cook: the host still smiles.
skill.insteadOf: I reject this offer.

weak: Refer me in your company.
strong: There's an analyst opening on your team that fits me — would you refer me? I can share my resume.
why: Naming the role and offering the resume makes referring a two-minute job.

skill.work: There's an analyst opening on your team; would you refer me? I'll send my CV.
skill.everyday: Could you put in a word with your society secretary? I'll call him.
skill.analogy: Like asking for a lift and naming the exact stop: it's easy to say yes.
skill.insteadOf: Refer me in your company.

weak: Give me the WiFi password.
strong: Could I get the WiFi password, please?
why: 'Could I get' plus 'please' turns a demand into a request guests are happy to meet.

skill.work: Could I get the guest Wi-Fi password, please?
skill.everyday: Could I get the Wi-Fi password, please? My data's run out.
skill.analogy: 'Could I' is like taking off your shoes at the door: small, but noticed.
skill.insteadOf: Give me the WiFi password.

weak: The food is not good.
strong: The curry is a touch too salty for me — but the dal is excellent.
why: One precise note inside genuine praise gets heard; blanket verdicts get dismissed.

skill.work: Priya: "How's the canteen biryani?" You: "A touch too salty for me, but the raita's great."
skill.everyday: Aunty: "How's the curry?" You: "A touch too salty for me, but the dal is excellent!"
skill.analogy: Like a review with one star off, not zero: honest, and still kind.
skill.insteadOf: The food is not good.

weak: Take my photo.
strong: Could you take a photo of us, please? Just press this button.
why: Framing it as one easy press makes strangers say yes instantly.

skill.work: Could you take a photo of the whiteboard before we wipe it?
skill.everyday: Could you take a photo of us, please? Just press this button.
skill.analogy: Like saying 'bhaiya' before asking directions: the softener makes people want to help.
skill.insteadOf: Take my photo.
